lines.text: Fountain pen tips were once miners' rubbish.
Soft gold wears away, so nibs got a hard osmiridium tip.
It is a natural alloy of osmium and iridium.
In the 1880s, Tasmanian gold miners kept finding it in their gold.
lines.say: In the eighteen eighties, Tasmanian gold miners kept finding it in their gold.

lines.text: They called it ossie and threw it away.
Then war and revolution cut off the Russian supply.
Tasmanian grains, the right size for nibs, sold for more than gold.
In 1925, over a thousand miner's rights were issued for Adamsfield.
lines.say: In nineteen twenty five, over a thousand miner's rights were issued for Adamsfield.

lines.text: Cheaper tip alloys and ballpoint pens ended the boom.
Many nibs still say iridium, but modern tips contain none.

post.caption: Fountain pen tips were once miners' rubbish. Soft gold wears away, so nibs got a hard osmiridium tip. It is a natural alloy of osmium and iridium. In the 1880s, Tasmanian gold miners kept finding it in their gold. They called it ossie and threw it away. Then war and revolution cut off the Russian supply. Tasmanian grains, the right size for nibs, sold for more than gold. In 1925, over a thousand miner's rights were issued for Adamsfield. Cheaper tip alloys and ballpoint pens ended the boom. Many nibs still say iridium, but modern tips contain none.
